title: Cerulean Health - Postmortem & Reliability Follow-up
summary: Postmortem follow-up covering last week's degradation that impacted Cerulean Health inference latency. Confirmed root cause as autoscaler race+KV cache eviction interaction on Dedicated cluster, discussed short-term mitigations (pin model, raised scaling thresholds, temporary routing to hosted), and agreed on longer-term changes: improved autoscaler heuristics, KV cache persistence, canary rollout for model swaps, and an on-prem runbook. Action items and timeline assigned.
next_steps: Redwood to share updated incident timeline and raw metrics (within 24h)
SE to run targeted load test with KV cache persistence toggled (by 2027-12-06)
Customer to approve test window for canary rollout (by 2027-12-03)
Exchange SSO logs and audit export for security review (Priya + Omar)
action_items: Owner: Jasper Lee | Item: Export autoscaler & nodegrouplogs + time-aligned KV cache metrics and send link | Due: 2027-11-30
Owner: Maya Thompson | Item: Consolidate pricing/contract impact for Dedicated burst during incident and share with Liam | Due: 2027-12-02
Owner: Anika Rao | Item: Confirm internal change window for canary and share calendar invite | Due: 2027-12-03
Owner: Omar Ruiz | Item: Share on-call escalation runbook template and draft on-prem rollback steps | Due: 2027-12-01
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-11-29 16:00 UTC | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Maya, Jasper, Omar (Redwood) / Anika, Liam, Priya, Ethan (Cerulean)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll get started. this is the postmortem follow-up for last thursday's degradation, goal is to walk through timeline, RCA, and next steps.
[00:18] Anika: thanks Maya. appreciate the quick turnaround on the initial notes. we had a pretty bad customer impact, latency spiked to, like, 8-12s for a bunch of our clinical workflows, which caused timeouts in the orchestration.
[00:35] Jasper: yeah sorry about that, team. from our preliminary look it looks like a confluence of the Dedicated autoscaler reacting to a noisy spike, combined with our KV cache eviction policy; the scale-up caused node churn and some requests missed the warm KV state.
[00:52] Liam: just to be clear: these were our production model endpoints on the dedicated cluster, not the hosted API, right?
[00:58] Maya: correct — Dedicated. you had model pinned to v3.1 but there was a split traffic canary we kicked off the same morning? i know we recommended canary but was the rollout manual or auto?
[01:12] Ethan: we kicked a canary at 06:30 for a small batch to validate inference output. hadn't expected it to interact with scaling but it did coincide with a monitoring alert window.
[01:27] Priya: and from security side we flagged the increased API retries; wanted to confirm if any PII was re-sent to external logs during the incident.
[01:36] Omar: good point — we verified no customer payloads left the VPC; logs are internal. we'll share the log export and audit markers.
[01:44] Anika: okay thanks. would like that for compliance.
[02:02] Jasper: walking through the timeline — at 06:29 we saw 2x baseline QPS for a 10 minute burst, autoscaler triggered a scale-up; at 06:33 there was a partial node rotation (some nodes drain), during drain the new nodes did not yet have warmed KV cache, so cold KV lookups hit model and increased latency; by 06:40 requests started failing their 5s client timeout causing retries and cascade.
[02:34] Liam: were the node drains graceful? our logs show evictions and some restarted processes.
[02:40] Jasper: we saw a mix; the orchestrator attempted graceful drain but a misconfigured probe threshold marked a few nodes unhealthy and killed pods earlier than expected. that's a config mismatch — probe threshold versus drain grace.
[02:56] Anika: is that a Redwood default or our cluster config?
[03:02] Jasper: the probe settings are inherited from the customer's cluster config; however our autoscaler recommends a grace period which we didn't enforce because the cluster had a custom kubelet flag. so responsibility is shared.
[03:20] Maya: makes sense — that's the kind of thing we want to document in the runbook. short-term mitigation we suggested yesterday was to pin the model and temporarily route traffic to hosted while we stabilize. did that help?
[03:33] Liam: yes routing ~30% to hosted during the incident brought median latency down to 600ms, but cost was higher and not sustainable long term.
[03:42] Anika: we also disabled the autoscaler which stopped churn but reduced capacity headroom — not ideal.
[03:49] Jasper: for immediate next steps, we recommend four items: 1) increase autoscaler cool-down and scale-up thresholds to avoid reacting to short bursts, 2) persist KV cache across node replacements (we have an experimental approach using local SSD-backed snapshot warmers), 3) change probe/grace configuration to be consistent with Redwood runtime expectations, and 4) implement canary rollout rules to avoid simultaneous canary + autoscale events.
[04:21] Priya: on KV cache persistence: what's the security model? does this persist to customer-managed storage? we can't allow PII to be written to shared storage.
[04:32] Jasper: yes — our approach for Dedicated is to persist to customer-owned ephemeral volumes encrypted with customer KMS where available; nothing goes to shared multi-tenant storage. we'll include details in the design doc.
[04:46] Priya: please put that in writing, we'll need it for our audit.
[04:52] Omar: will do; we'll attach encryption and retention details.
[05:10] Anika: also, can you send the full incident timeline with raw metrics? the summary was helpful but we need the time-aligned CSVs for our runbook.
[05:20] Jasper: yes will export the autoscaler events, node rotations, and KV cache miss rates — we'll upload to the shared folder.
[05:29] Maya: quick question about SLA credits — do we have an estimate of how this maps to the committed monthly uptime?
[05:37] Omar: i'll coordinate with RevOps and get a preliminary impact analysis; depends on exact outage window we agree on, we'll follow contract terms.
[05:45] Liam: from our side the critical ask is preventing recurrence. what does a more durable design look like?
[05:52] Jasper: long-term: 1) autoscaler heuristics that consider KV warmness metrics before scaling down/in; 2) persistent KV layer or warmers that hydrate new nodes; 3) canary gating tied to capacity signals; 4) better tracing to identify cross-service retries. We can propose prioritization and timelines.
[06:18] Ethan: about tracing — our tracing sampling rate is low; during the incident we missed some traces. will need higher sampling for infra signals.
[06:26] Maya: we can help instrument extra trace hooks for the short window of the upcoming test.
[06:31] Anika: i'd like to schedule the load test Jasper mentioned — can we do that next week in a low-traffic window?
[06:38] Jasper: yes targeting 2027-12-06 (US overnight) per notes. will send a test plan.
[06:45] Priya: will security review the test plan? want to ensure no data exfil during tests.
[06:50] Omar: yes we'll include safe test inputs and mask PHI fields.
[07:02] Maya: ok let's go over the agreed action owners (quick recap)
[07:08] Anika: we also have a question — if KV cache persistence requires local SSD on nodes, do we need a dedicated instance type? cost implications?
[07:18] Jasper: potentially, yes. there's a tradeoff: SSD-backed nodes increase infra cost but reduce runtime token cost by avoiding recomputation. we'll model cost in the design doc.
[07:31] Liam: we'd rather pay a predictable infra uplift than have intermittent timeouts.
[07:35] Maya: noted. we'll include cost scenarios.
[07:44] Priya: also request: please add a security appendix for the postmortem with KMS key IDs and retention policies redacted, we need to attach to ticket.
[07:55] Omar: will prepare that and share under the secure folder.
[08:06] Jasper: final technical note: we discovered an internal bug in our warmup logic where concurrent warmers could evict each other's state under certain race conditions — small fix, unit tests on it are already in review.
[08:20] Ethan: great to hear. any ETA on the patch?
[08:23] Jasper: patch merged to staging; we aim to push to prod after the load test validation, target 2027-12-08.
[08:30] Anika: ok thanks, that helps.
[08:36] Maya: let's confirm deliverables and dates: Jasper uploads metrics by 11/30; Jasper run load test 12/06; patch to prod 12/08; Maya consolidates cost/pricing 12/02; Anika approves canary by 12/03; Omar sends runbook 12/01.
[08:58] Liam: sounds good. thanks everyone for the quick action.
[09:05] Priya: and please keep us in the loop on the SLA credit evaluation.
[09:10] Omar: noted. we'll follow up with RevOps.
[09:20] Maya: any other questions?
[09:25] Anika: no, we're good. thank you.
[09:30] Maya: thanks all — we'll share notes and artifacts right after this.

[End of transcript]
